record.original_question: Among all connected one-dimensional armatures Γ of prescribed total length L in three-dimensional space, maximize the volume of the convex hull of Γ. The best candidate reported in the article is a helical arc (the Nudel'man curve), and the open question is whether that helical armature is in fact an optimal solution to the 3D problem in full generality.

evidence.quote: Le problème est de trouver une armature unidimensionnelle connexe Γ, de longueur totale fixée L, telle que son enveloppe convexe est d’aire ou volume maximal.

En 3D, ce qu’on a trouvé de mieux est une armature Γ* en forme d’arc hélicoïdal (appelée encore courbe de Nudel’man ([6])), d’équations paramétriques : x(t) = cos t ; y(t) = sin t ; z(t) = 1/√2 t ∈ [0, 2π].
De fait, on conjecture que cet arc hélicoïdal est solution du problème posé, dans toute sa généralité.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a connected one-dimensional rectifiable set (an "armature"; e.g., a finite connected union of rectifiable arcs) of prescribed total one-dimensional length $\mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma) = L > 0$. Let $\operatorname{conv}(\Gamma)$ denote its convex hull and $\operatorname{vol}_3$ the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Consider the optimization problem
$$ V(L) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\,\operatorname{vol}_3(\operatorname{conv}(\Gamma)) : \Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \text{ connected, } \mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma)=L\,\bigr\}. $$
A candidate extremal armature is the helical arc $\Gamma^*$ (Nudel'man curve) given parametrically (up to scaling so that its length equals $L$) by
$$ x(t) = \cos t,\quad y(t)=\sin t,\quad z(t) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,t, \qquad t \in [0, 2\pi]. $$
Prove or disprove: this helical arc $\Gamma^*$ attains the supremum $V(L)$, i.e., it is a global maximizer of the convex-hull volume among all connected one-dimensional armatures of total length $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface any published proof or disproof that the Nudel'man helical arc maximizes the convex-hull volume among connected one-dimensional armatures of fixed length in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Related work on convex hulls of space curves exists (e.g., on Frenet curves and isoperimetric problems for closed space curves), but none directly resolves this conjecture, which is described as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Convex Hulls of Curves: Volumes and Signatures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies volumes of convex hulls of space curves, but does not address the helical-armature optimality conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature treats convex-hull volumes of curves without resolving the Nudel'man helix conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The convex hull of a convex space curve with four vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Considers convex hulls of certain Frenet curves; unrelated to the fixed-length maximization in 3D.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the helical optimality is given in the related convex-hull-of-curves literature.
